hints: Look at the scale bar under the photo. Measure its length on the page in mm with a ruler, that is your image size.
Remember magnification = image size divided by actual size, so you must convert your mm measurement to micrometres first.
walkthrough:
**Measure the image size**

Grab a ruler and measure the printed 5 um scale bar. It is about 20 mm long on the page.

This 20 mm is the magnified image size of something that is really only 5 um long.

**Make the units match**

You cannot divide mm by um directly, so convert mm to um first.

Key conversion:
$$1 \text{ mm} = 1000 \text{ } \mu\text{m}$$
So:
$$20 \text{ mm} \times 1000 = 20000 \text{ } \mu\text{m}$$

**Apply the magnification formula**

Now use the golden rule for all microscopy maths:
$$\text{magnification} = \frac{\text{image size}}{\text{actual size}}$$
Put the numbers in:
$$\text{magnification} = \frac{20000 \text{ } \mu\text{m}}{5 \text{ } \mu\text{m}} = 4000$$
So the image is 4000 times bigger than real life, which is x4000.

options.A: x250 is far too small. It would make the 5 um bar only 1.25 mm long on the page, but it is much longer than that.
options.B: x400 is still too small. It would make the 5 um bar only 2 mm long, which does not match the measured bar.
options.C: x1000 would make the 5 um bar only 5 mm long. The bar in the photo is about four times longer than this.
options.D: x4000 is correct because a 20 mm image size divided by a 5 um actual size (20000 um / 5 um) gives 4000.
